256-bit j=0 curve with prime order and twist 3*prime (best possible twist security for j=0)
Curve: y^2 = x^3 + b over GF(p), p == 1 (mod 3), p = x^2 + 3*y^2 (random, no special form)

p  = 74515312981217264957709166294531260962117627716569960380215249868496272297899
b  = 13
G  = (47297481605411866015687003603476059640678532764580237070245035833752246220180,
      6515249504229895111059500307307677041530907606728679469134815945529511636901)
n  = 74515312981217264957709166294531260962632445609123029240215655821140364170413      (prime, order of G, cofactor 1)
twist order = 2*(p+1) - n = 3*q,  q = 24838437660405754985903055431510420320534269941338963840071614638617393475129  (prime)
twist curve: y^2 = x^3 + b*d^3 with d = 2 (quadratic non-residue)

Checks done (Python/sympy): p, n, q prime; G on curve; n*G = infinity (so #E = n exactly);
n' = 3q kills a random point of the twist; n != p (not anomalous); embedding degree > 200000.

PARI/GP verification:
p = 74515312981217264957709166294531260962117627716569960380215249868496272297899;
n = 74515312981217264957709166294531260962632445609123029240215655821140364170413;
q = 24838437660405754985903055431510420320534269941338963840071614638617393475129;
E = ellinit([0,13], p);
print(isprime(p), isprime(n), isprime(q));
print(ellcard(E) == n);
print(2*(p+1) - n == 3*q);
print(ellmul(E, [47297481605411866015687003603476059640678532764580237070245035833752246220180,6515249504229895111059500307307677041530907606728679469134815945529511636901], n) == [0]);

Notes: p is random (not a special-form prime), so field arithmetic is slower than for secp256k1; the CM discriminant is -3 (inherent to j=0); this is a demonstration, not a standard curve.
